source.text: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς δώδεκα μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων ὥστε ἐκβάλλειν αὐτὰ καὶ θεραπεύειν πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν.

records.literal_gloss: And having summoned the twelve disciples of him he gave to them authority over spirits unclean so as to cast out them and to heal every disease and every sickness.

en.L: And summoning {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve disciples, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them authority over unclean spirits, so as to cast them out and to heal every disease and every sickness.
en.B: Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve disciples to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to drive them out, and to heal every disease and every illness.
en.R: Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve followers together. He gave them power over evil spirits so that they could make the spirits leave people. He also gave them power to heal every kind of sickness and disease.

es.L: Y habiendo convocado a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} doce discípulos, les dio autoridad sobre espíritus impuros, de modo que los expulsaran y curaran toda enfermedad y todo mal.
es.B: Jesús llamó junto a {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} doce discípulos y les dio autoridad sobre los espíritus impuros, para expulsarlos y para curar toda clase de enfermedades y dolencias.
es.R: Jesús reunió a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} doce seguidores. Les dio poder sobre los espíritus malignos, para que pudieran hacerlos salir de las personas. También les dio poder para sanar toda clase de enfermedades y dolencias.

sw.L: Na baada ya kuwaita wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kumi na wawili, aliwapa mamlaka juu ya pepo wachafu, ili kuwafukuza na kuponya kila ugonjwa na kila udhaifu.
sw.B: Yesu aliwaita {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kumi na wawili, akawapa mamlaka juu ya pepo wachafu, wawafukuze, na waponye kila aina ya ugonjwa na maradhi.
sw.R: Yesu aliwakusanya pamoja wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kumi na wawili. Aliwapa uwezo juu ya pepo wabaya, ili waweze kuwafukuza kutoka kwa watu. Pia aliwapa uwezo wa kuponya kila aina ya magonjwa na maradhi.

decisions.choice: authority over unclean spirits: the right and power to command them
decisions.reason: The genitive names what the authority is over. The next words say what it is for: to cast the spirits out.

decisions.choice: every disease and every sickness: the same words as 4:23 and 9:35
decisions.reason: Matthew describes the twelve's work in the words he used for Jesus's own work. They share in what he does.

decisions.choice: unclean spirits: demons
decisions.reason: Unclean spirits are the demons of 10:8. They are unclean because they are opposed to God and defile those they control.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins here, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: evil spirits
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer phrase for the same beings.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives (sus, sí, lo, mí)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out ("dio", "envió") and joins some object pronouns to the verb ("seguirme"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise, so the setting covers fewer words than in English. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: espíritus impuros (L, B); espíritus malignos (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts. "Inmundo" is the traditional word but now sounds like dirt; "impuro" says the spirits make a person unfit to come near God, and Readable says plainly that they are evil, as the English does (meaning decision m3). "Toda enfermedad y todo mal" repeats the wording of 9:35 (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (wake, kwake, yangu)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Swahili carries most pronouns in the verb ("aliwapa", "alimsaliti"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, as in John and Mark. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: pepo wachafu (L, B); pepo wabaya (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts for unclean spirits, which are demons (meaning decision m3); Readable says plainly that they are evil, as the English does. "Kila ugonjwa na kila udhaifu" repeats the wording of 9:35 (meaning decision m2).

source.text: τῶν δὲ δώδεκα ἀποστόλων τὰ ὀνόματά ἐστιν ταῦτα· πρῶτος Σίμων ὁ λεγόμενος Πέτρος καὶ Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ, Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννης ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ, Φίλιππος καὶ Βαρθολομαῖος, Θωμᾶς καὶ Μαθθαῖος ὁ τελώνης, Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καὶ Θαδδαῖος, Σίμων ὁ Καναναῖος καὶ Ἰούδας ὁ Ἰσκαριώτης ὁ καὶ παραδοὺς αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Of the and twelve apostles the names are these: first Simon the [one] called Peter and Andrew the brother of him, James the [son] of Zebedee and John the brother of him, \v 3 Philip and Bartholomew, Thomas and Matthew the tax collector, James the [son] of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus, \v 4 Simon the Cananaean and Judas the Iscariot the [one] also having betrayed him.

en.L: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: first, Simon, the [one] called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the [son] of Zebedee, and John his brother; \v 3 Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James the [son] of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus; \v 4 Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, the [one] who also betrayed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The twelve apostles were these. First came Simon, known as Peter, with his brother Andrew; then James son of Zebedee, with his brother John; \v 3 Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus; \v 4 Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, the man who betrayed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Here are the names of the twelve apostles. First was Simon, who was also called Peter. Then there was his brother Andrew. There were James and his brother John, the sons of Zebedee. \v 3 There were Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, and Matthew the tax collector. There were James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus. \v 4 And there were Simon the Zealot and Judas Iscariot. Judas was the one who later betrayed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y los nombres de los doce apóstoles son estos: primero, Simón, el llamado Pedro, y Andrés su hermano; Santiago el [hijo] de Zebedeo, y Juan su hermano; \v 3 Felipe y Bartolomé; Tomás y Mateo el publicano; Santiago el [hijo] de Alfeo, y Tadeo; \v 4 Simón el cananista, y Judas el Iscariote, el que también {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregó.
es.B: Estos son los nombres de los doce apóstoles. Primero, Simón, llamado Pedro, con su hermano Andrés; luego Santiago, hijo de Zebedeo, con su hermano Juan; \v 3 Felipe y Bartolomé; Tomás y Mateo, el cobrador de impuestos; Santiago, hijo de Alfeo, y Tadeo; \v 4 Simón el cananista y Judas Iscariote, el que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} traicionó.
es.R: Estos son los nombres de los doce apóstoles. El primero era Simón, al que también llamaban Pedro. Después estaba su hermano Andrés. Estaban Santiago y su hermano Juan, los hijos de Zebedeo. \v 3 Estaban Felipe, Bartolomé, Tomás y Mateo, el cobrador de impuestos. Estaban Santiago, hijo de Alfeo, y Tadeo. \v 4 Y estaban Simón el Zelote y Judas Iscariote. Judas fue el que más tarde {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} traicionó.

sw.L: Basi majina ya mitume kumi na wawili ni haya: wa kwanza, Simoni, aitwaye Petro, na Andrea ndugu yake; Yakobo [mwana] wa Zebedayo, na Yohana ndugu yake; \v 3 Filipo na Bartholomayo; Tomaso na Mathayo mtoza ushuru; Yakobo [mwana] wa Alfayo, na Thadayo; \v 4 Simoni Mkananayo, na Yuda Iskariote, ambaye pia alimsaliti.
sw.B: Mitume kumi na wawili walikuwa hawa: wa kwanza Simoni, aliyeitwa Petro, pamoja na ndugu yake Andrea; kisha Yakobo mwana wa Zebedayo, pamoja na ndugu yake Yohana; \v 3 Filipo na Bartholomayo; Tomaso, na Mathayo mtoza ushuru; Yakobo mwana wa Alfayo, na Thadayo; \v 4 Simoni Mkananayo, na Yuda Iskariote, yule aliyemsaliti.
sw.R: Haya ndiyo majina ya wale mitume kumi na wawili. Wa kwanza alikuwa Simoni, ambaye pia aliitwa Petro. Kisha alikuwepo ndugu yake Andrea. Walikuwepo Yakobo na ndugu yake Yohana, wana wa Zebedayo. \v 3 Walikuwepo Filipo, Bartholomayo, Tomaso, na Mathayo mtoza ushuru. Walikuwepo Yakobo mwana wa Alfayo, na Thadayo. \v 4 Tena walikuwepo Simoni Mzelote na Yuda Iskariote. Yuda ndiye ambaye baadaye alimsaliti.

decisions.choice: apostles: those sent out with authority to act for the one who sends them
decisions.reason: This is the only place Matthew uses the word. It comes from the verb "send out" used in 10:5 and 10:16.

decisions.choice: first: Peter heads the list
alternatives: the first one called, with no further sense
decisions.reason: Peter is named first in every list of the twelve (Mark 3:16; Luke 6:14; Acts 1:13), and he often speaks for them (16:16; 19:27).

decisions.choice: the Cananaean: from an Aramaic word meaning zealot, one zealous for God
decisions.reason: Luke 6:15 and Acts 1:13 call him "the Zealot". Whether this marks him as one who had fought against Roman rule or as one zealous for the law is not clear.

decisions.choice: Thaddaeus, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Lebbaeus, or Lebbaeus called Thaddaeus, the reading of some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "Lebbaeus" here, and many later ones combine the two names. Luke 6:16 and Acts 1:13 name "Judas son of James" in this place in the list. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: betrayed: handed over to his enemies
decisions.reason: The verb means to hand over. Matthew uses it for Judas giving Jesus up (26:15-16) and for the disciples' own arrest (10:17, 19, 21). The meaning of "Iscariot" is not certain; it may mean "man from Kerioth".

decisions.choice: Simon the Zealot (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the name as Matthew gives it; Readable gives its meaning, as Luke does.

decisions.choice: el cananista (L, B); el Zelote (R)
decisions.reason: The word comes from Aramaic and means a zealot (meaning decision m3, uncertain). Spanish "cananeo" means a Canaanite, a different people, so Literal and Balanced use the distinct form "cananista"; Readable gives the meaning, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: el publicano (L); el cobrador de impuestos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "publicano" is the traditional name for these tax farmers; Balanced and Readable say what Matthew's work was.

decisions.choice: Simoni Mkananayo (L, B); Simoni Mzelote (R)
decisions.reason: The word comes from Aramaic and means a zealot (meaning decision m3, uncertain). "Mkanaani" would make him a Canaanite, a different people, so Literal and Balanced keep the form of the Greek name; Readable gives the meaning, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: mitume
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "mtume" is one sent out with authority to act for the one who sends him (meaning decision m1).

source.text: Τούτους τοὺς δώδεκα ἀπέστειλεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς παραγγείλας αὐτοῖς λέγων· Εἰς ὁδὸν ἐθνῶν μὴ ἀπέλθητε καὶ εἰς πόλιν Σαμαριτῶν μὴ εἰσέλθητε·

records.literal_gloss: These the twelve sent out the Jesus having instructed them saying, Into a road of Gentiles not go off, and into a town of Samaritans not enter;

en.L: These twelve Jesus sent out, instructing them, saying, "Do not go off onto [the] road of [the] Gentiles, and do not enter a town of [the] Samaritans;
en.B: Jesus sent these twelve out, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} charged them: "Stay off the roads that lead to the Gentiles, and do not go into any Samaritan town.
en.R: Jesus sent out these twelve men. First {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them what to do: "Do not go to people who are not Jews. And do not go into any town where Samaritans live.

es.L: A estos doce los envió Jesús, mandándoles: «No {{plural_you:tomen|toméis}} [el] camino de [los] gentiles, ni {{plural_you:entren|entréis}} en [ningún] pueblo de samaritanos;
es.B: Jesús envió a estos doce con estas órdenes: «No {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} por los caminos que llevan a los gentiles, ni {{plural_you:entren|entréis}} en ningún pueblo samaritano.
es.R: Jesús envió a estos doce hombres. Primero les explicó lo que tenían que hacer: «No {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} adonde vive gente que no es judía. Y no {{plural_you:entren|entréis}} en ningún pueblo donde vivan samaritanos.

sw.L: Hao kumi na wawili Yesu aliwatuma nje, akiwapa maagizo, akisema, "Msigeuke kufuata njia ya watu wa mataifa, wala msiingie mji wa Wasamaria;
sw.B: Yesu aliwatuma hao kumi na wawili, akawapa maagizo haya: "Msishike njia zinazoelekea kwa watu wa mataifa, wala msiingie mji wa Kisamaria.
sw.R: Yesu aliwatuma watu hao kumi na wawili. Kwanza aliwaeleza la kufanya: "Msiende kwa watu wasio Wayahudi. Wala msiingie mji wowote wanamoishi Wasamaria.

decisions.choice: the road of the Gentiles: a road leading into Gentile country
decisions.reason: The words speak of a journey's direction. The twelve are not to take their mission beyond Israel.

decisions.choice: Samaritans: the people of Samaria, between Judea and Galilee
decisions.reason: The Samaritans worshiped the God of Israel but had their own temple and form of the law, and Jews and Samaritans were bitterly divided (John 4:9).

decisions.choice: a limit for this mission, not for all time
alternatives: a rule that the gospel is only for Israel
decisions.reason: Jesus comes first to Israel (15:24). After his resurrection he sends his disciples to all nations (28:19).

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable says who the Gentiles are, as in 4:15.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 10:42
alternatives: closing and reopening the quotation at each sentence
decisions.reason: Verses 5-42 are one speech, so the quotation marks stay open to the end.

decisions.choice: gentiles (L, B); gente que no es judía (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "gentiles" names the peoples who are not Israel; Readable says it plainly, as the English does (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every verb and pronoun addressed to the Twelve; the « opens here and stays open to the end of 10:42
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them, and English has no such choice. Jesus speaks from here to 10:42, so the words he quotes inside take “ ”, as the English puts them in single marks.

decisions.choice: watu wa mataifa (L, B); watu wasio Wayahudi (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts for the peoples who are not Israel; Readable says it plainly, as the English does (meaning decision m1). Jesus speaks from here to 10:42, so the quotation stays open, and the words he quotes inside take single marks.

source.text: πορεύεσθε δὲ μᾶλλον πρὸς τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἀπολωλότα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ.

records.literal_gloss: go but rather to the sheep the being lost of house of Israel.

en.L: but go rather to the lost sheep of [the] house of Israel.
en.B: Go instead to the lost sheep, the people of Israel.
en.R: Go to the people of Israel. They are like sheep that are lost.

es.L: sino {{plural_you:diríjanse|dirigíos}} más bien a las ovejas perdidas de [la] casa de Israel.
es.B: {{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} más bien a las ovejas perdidas, al pueblo de Israel.
es.R: {{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} al pueblo de Israel. Son como ovejas perdidas.

sw.L: bali afadhali nendeni kwa kondoo waliopotea wa nyumba ya Israeli.
sw.B: Badala yake nendeni kwa kondoo waliopotea, yaani watu wa Israeli.
sw.R: Nendeni kwa watu wa Israeli. Wao ni kama kondoo waliopotea.

decisions.choice: the lost sheep, the house of Israel: the whole people is the lost flock
alternatives: only the lost ones within Israel
decisions.reason: As in 9:36, Jesus sees Israel as sheep without a shepherd. The same words come again in 15:24.

decisions.choice: lost sheep: Jeremiah 50:6; Ezekiel 34:4, 16
decisions.reason: The prophets call Israel lost sheep led astray by their shepherds, and God promises to seek the lost.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: "House" means the whole family or nation.

source.text: πορευόμενοι δὲ κηρύσσετε λέγοντες ὅτι Ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Going and proclaim saying that, Has come near the kingdom of the heavens.

en.L: And as you go, proclaim, saying, 'The kingdom of the heavens has come near.'
en.B: Wherever you go, preach this: 'The kingdom of heaven has come near.'
en.R: As you travel, tell people, 'The kingdom of heaven is coming near.'

es.L: Y mientras {{plural_you:van|vais}}, {{plural_you:proclamen|proclamad}}, diciendo: “Se ha acercado el reino de los cielos”.
es.B: Por dondequiera que {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}}, {{plural_you:anuncien|anunciad}} esto: “El reino de los cielos se ha acercado”.
es.R: Mientras {{plural_you:viajan|viajáis}}, {{plural_you:digan|decid}} a la gente: “El reino de los cielos se está acercando”.

sw.L: Na mkienda, hubirini, mkisema, 'Ufalme wa mbinguni umekuja karibu.'
sw.B: Popote mwendapo, hubirini hivi: 'Ufalme wa mbinguni uko karibu.'
sw.R: Mnaposafiri, waambieni watu, 'Ufalme wa mbinguni unakaribia.'

decisions.choice: the same message as John's and Jesus's (3:2; 4:17)
decisions.reason: The twelve announce what Jesus announced. See 3:2 on "the kingdom of heaven".

decisions.choice: the same wording as 4:17 at each level
decisions.reason: The repeated message is given in the same words.

decisions.choice: el reino de los cielos
decisions.reason: The term used throughout Matthew: Matthew's way of saying "the kingdom of God", keeping the plural of the Greek as Spanish usage does.

decisions.choice: ufalme wa mbinguni
decisions.reason: The term used throughout Matthew, his way of saying "the kingdom of God". "Mbinguni" (in heaven) is the natural Swahili form.

source.text: ἀσθενοῦντας θεραπεύετε, νεκροὺς ἐγείρετε, λεπροὺς καθαρίζετε, δαιμόνια ἐκβάλλετε· δωρεὰν ἐλάβετε, δωρεὰν δότε.

records.literal_gloss: Ailing heal, dead raise, lepers cleanse, demons cast out; freely you received, freely give.

en.L: Heal [the] sick, raise [the] dead, cleanse lepers, cast out demons. Freely you received; freely give.
en.B: Heal those who are sick, raise the dead, make lepers clean, drive out demons. You received without paying, so give without charging.
en.R: Heal sick people. Bring dead people back to life. Heal people who have skin diseases. Make demons leave people. You did not pay for what you were given, so do not ask people to pay you.

es.L: {{plural_you:Sanen|Sanad}} enfermos, {{plural_you:resuciten|resucitad}} muertos, {{plural_you:limpien|limpiad}} leprosos, {{plural_you:expulsen|expulsad}} demonios. Gratis {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}}; {{plural_you:den|dad}} gratis.
es.B: {{plural_you:Sanen|Sanad}} a los enfermos, {{plural_you:resuciten|resucitad}} a los muertos, {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} limpios a los leprosos, {{plural_you:echen|echad}} fuera a los demonios. {{plural_you:Recibieron|Recibisteis}} sin pagar; {{plural_you:den|dad}} sin cobrar.
es.R: {{plural_you:Sanen|Sanad}} a los enfermos. {{plural_you:Devuelvan|Devolved}} la vida a los muertos. {{plural_you:Sanen|Sanad}} a los que tienen enfermedades de la piel. {{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} salir a los demonios de la gente. {{plural_you:Ustedes no pagaron|Vosotros no pagasteis}} por lo que {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}}, así que no {{plural_you:pidan|pidáis}} a nadie que {{plural_you:les|os}} pague.

sw.L: Wagonjwa waponyeni, wafu wafufueni, wenye ukoma watakaseni, pepo wafukuzeni. Bila malipo mlipokea; bila malipo toeni.
sw.B: Waponyeni wagonjwa, wafufueni waliokufa, watakaseni wenye ukoma, wafukuzeni pepo. Mlipokea bila kulipa, kwa hiyo toeni bila kudai malipo.
sw.R: Waponyeni wagonjwa. Wafufueni waliokufa. Waponyeni watu wenye magonjwa ya ngozi. Wafukuzeni pepo watoke kwa watu. Hamkulipa kwa yale mliyopewa, kwa hiyo msiwadai watu malipo.

decisions.choice: cleanse lepers: heal skin diseases that made a person unclean
alternatives: leprosy in the modern medical sense only
decisions.reason: As in 8:2-3, the word covered several skin diseases. Healing also made the person clean, able to return to worship and community.

decisions.choice: freely: as a gift, without payment
decisions.reason: The twelve received their power from Jesus at no cost, so they must not sell it. Compare Acts 8:18-20.

decisions.choice: raise the dead, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the words are missing in many later manuscripts, and their place varies in others
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts lack "raise the dead", and others place it differently in the list. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: people who have skin diseases
decisions.reason: Readable describes the condition, as in 8:2.

decisions.choice: objects first: Wagonjwa waponyeni, wafu wafufueni
decisions.reason: Swahili can put the object first, with the object prefix in the verb, so Literal keeps the Greek order, where each command begins with the people it is for.

source.text: μὴ κτήσησθε χρυσὸν μηδὲ ἄργυρον μηδὲ χαλκὸν εἰς τὰς ζώνας ὑμῶν, μὴ πήραν εἰς ὁδὸν μηδὲ δύο χιτῶνας μηδὲ ὑποδήματα μηδὲ ῥάβδον· ἄξιος γὰρ ὁ ἐργάτης τῆς τροφῆς αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Not acquire gold nor silver nor copper in the belts of you, \v 10 not a bag for road nor two tunics nor sandals nor a staff; worthy for the worker of the food of him.

en.L: Do not acquire gold or silver or copper for your belts, \v 10 nor a bag for [the] road, nor two tunics, nor sandals, nor a staff; for the worker [is] worthy of {{gender:their|his}} food.
en.B: Do not provide yourselves with money for your belts, whether gold, silver, or copper. \v 10 Take no bag for the road, no second tunic, no sandals, and no staff. Workers have earned their food.
en.R: Do not take any money with you, not gold or silver or even copper coins. \v 10 Do not take a bag for the trip, or extra clothes, or sandals, or a walking stick. People who work should be given food. The people you serve will take care of you.

es.L: No {{plural_you:adquieran|adquiráis}} oro, ni plata, ni cobre para {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} cinturones, \v 10 ni alforja para [el] camino, ni dos túnicas, ni sandalias, ni bastón; pues digno [es] el trabajador de su sustento.
es.B: No {{plural_you:se procuren|os procuréis}} dinero para el cinturón, sea oro, plata o cobre. \v 10 No {{plural_you:lleven|llevéis}} bolsa para el viaje, ni túnica de repuesto, ni sandalias, ni bastón. Quien trabaja se ha ganado su comida.
es.R: No {{plural_you:lleven|llevéis}} dinero, ni oro, ni plata, ni siquiera monedas de cobre. \v 10 No {{plural_you:lleven|llevéis}} bolsa para el viaje, ni ropa de repuesto, ni sandalias, ni bastón para caminar. Al que trabaja se le debe dar de comer. La gente a la que {{plural_you:sirvan|sirváis}} se ocupará de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Msijipatie dhahabu wala fedha wala shaba katika mikanda yenu, \v 10 wala mkoba kwa ajili ya njia, wala mavazi ya ndani mawili, wala viatu, wala fimbo; kwa maana mfanyakazi anastahili chakula chake.
sw.B: Msijipatie pesa za kuweka mikandani mwenu, iwe dhahabu, fedha au shaba. \v 10 Msichukue mkoba wa safari, wala vazi la pili, wala viatu, wala fimbo. Mfanyakazi amestahili chakula chake.
sw.R: Msichukue pesa yoyote, iwe dhahabu, fedha, au hata sarafu za shaba. \v 10 Msichukue mkoba wa safari, wala nguo za ziada, wala viatu, wala fimbo ya kutembelea. Watu wanaofanya kazi wanapaswa kupewa chakula. Watu mnaowahudumia watawatunza.

decisions.choice: acquire: get or provide for yourselves for the journey
decisions.reason: The verb means to get or procure. With 10:8 it may also forbid making money from the mission, but the list that follows is about what to take.

decisions.choice: gold, silver, copper in your belts: money of any kind
decisions.reason: Coins were carried in a fold of the belt. Copper coins were the smallest change, so the list rules out money altogether.

decisions.choice: a bag, a second tunic, a staff: the gear of a traveler
decisions.reason: A traveler carried a bag for food, a spare tunic for the cold, and a staff for walking and defense. Mark 6:8-9 allows a staff and sandals; Matthew and Luke 9:3 have Jesus forbid them. Each Gospel stresses that the twelve are to travel light and depend on God.

decisions.choice: the worker is worthy of his food: those they serve should feed them
alternatives: they must earn food by other work
decisions.reason: This is the reason for going without supplies. Luke 10:7 has "wages", and Paul cites the saying (1 Corinthians 9:14; 1 Timothy 5:18).

decisions.choice: The people you serve will take care of you.
decisions.reason: Readable states how the saying applies to the twelve.

decisions.choice: su sustento, su comida, with no gender span
decisions.reason: English needs a gender span for "their" or "his" food; Spanish "su" serves for a man or a woman, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: mfanyakazi ... chakula chake, with no gender span
decisions.reason: English needs a gender span for "their" or "his" food; Swahili "mfanyakazi" and "chake" serve for a man or a woman, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

source.text: εἰς ἣν δ’ ἂν πόλιν ἢ κώμην εἰσέλθητε, ἐξετάσατε τίς ἐν αὐτῇ ἄξιός ἐστιν· κἀκεῖ μείνατε ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθητε.

records.literal_gloss: Into whatever now town or village you enter, inquire who in it worthy is; and there remain until you go out.

en.L: And into whatever town or village you enter, inquire who in it is worthy, and stay there until you go out.
en.B: When you go into a town or village, ask who in it is worthy, and stay with that person until you move on.
en.R: When you come to a town or village, find someone there who is ready to welcome you. Stay in that person's home until you leave that place.

es.L: Y en cualquier ciudad o aldea en que {{plural_you:entren|entréis}}, {{plural_you:averigüen|averiguad}} quién en ella es digno, y {{plural_you:quédense|quedaos}} allí hasta que {{plural_you:salgan|salgáis}}.
es.B: Cuando {{plural_you:entren|entréis}} en una ciudad o aldea, {{plural_you:pregunten|preguntad}} quién es digno allí, y {{plural_you:quédense|quedaos}} en su casa hasta que {{plural_you:se vayan|os vayáis}}.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:lleguen|lleguéis}} a una ciudad o aldea, {{plural_you:busquen|buscad}} a alguien que esté dispuesto a {{plural_you:recibirlos|recibiros}}. {{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} en su casa hasta que {{plural_you:salgan|salgáis}} de ese lugar.

sw.L: Na mji au kijiji chochote mtakachoingia, ulizeni ni nani ndani yake anayestahili; na hapo kaeni hadi mtakapoondoka.
sw.B: Mkiingia katika mji au kijiji, ulizeni ni nani humo anayestahili, mkae kwake mpaka mtakapoendelea na safari.
sw.R: Mkifika katika mji au kijiji, mtafuteni mtu aliye tayari kuwakaribisha. Kaeni nyumbani kwake mpaka mtakapoondoka mahali hapo.

decisions.choice: worthy: open to the message and ready to receive the messengers
decisions.reason: The worthy house is the one that receives them and their words (10:13-14).

decisions.choice: stay there: do not move from house to house
decisions.reason: They are to lodge in one home for their whole stay in that place.

decisions.choice: someone ... who is ready to welcome you
decisions.reason: Readable says what "worthy" means here.

source.text: εἰσερχόμενοι δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν ἀσπάσασθε αὐτήν·

records.literal_gloss: Entering now into the house greet it;

en.L: And as you enter the house, greet it;
en.B: As you go into the home, greet the family.
en.R: When you go into a home, say, 'Peace be with you.'

es.L: Y al entrar en la casa, {{plural_you:salúdenla|saludadla}};
es.B: Al entrar en la casa, {{plural_you:saluden|saludad}} a la familia.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:entren|entréis}} en una casa, {{plural_you:digan|decid}}: “La paz sea con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}”.

sw.L: Na mnapoingia katika nyumba, isalimuni;
sw.B: Mnapoingia nyumbani, wasalimuni watu wa nyumba hiyo.
sw.R: Mnapoingia katika nyumba, semeni, 'Amani iwe nanyi.'

decisions.choice: the house: the household, the people who live there
decisions.reason: A greeting is given to people, as 10:13 shows.

decisions.choice: greet it, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: some manuscripts add "saying, Peace to this house"
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts add the words of the greeting, as in Luke 10:5. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: say, 'Peace be with you'
decisions.reason: The usual greeting was a wish for peace, as 10:13 implies. Readable gives it.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν μὲν ᾖ ἡ οἰκία ἀξία, ἐλθάτω ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν ἐπ’ αὐτήν· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ᾖ ἀξία, ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐπιστραφήτω.

records.literal_gloss: And if indeed be the house worthy, let come the peace of you upon it; if but not it be worthy, the peace of you to you let return.

en.L: And if the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; but if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.
en.B: If that household is worthy, let your peace come to rest on it. But if it is unworthy, let the peace you gave come back to you.
en.R: If the people in that home welcome you, your blessing of peace will stay with them. If they do not welcome you, your blessing will come back to you.

es.L: Y si la casa es digna, venga sobre ella {{plural_you:la paz de ustedes|vuestra paz}}; pero si no es digna, {{plural_you:la paz de ustedes|vuestra paz}} vuelva a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Si esa familia es digna, que repose sobre ella la paz que {{plural_you:ustedes le desean|vosotros le deseáis}}. Pero si no lo es, que esa paz vuelva a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Si la gente de esa casa {{plural_you:los|os}} recibe bien, la paz que {{plural_you:ustedes les desean|vosotros les deseáis}} se quedará con ellos. Si no {{plural_you:los|os}} reciben, esa bendición volverá a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Na kama kweli nyumba hiyo ni yenye kustahili, amani yenu ije juu yake; lakini kama si yenye kustahili, amani yenu irudi kwenu.
sw.B: Ikiwa watu wa nyumba hiyo wanastahili, amani mnayowatakia ikae juu yao. Lakini kama hawastahili, amani mliyotoa irudi kwenu.
sw.R: Kama watu wa nyumba hiyo watawakaribisha, baraka yenu ya amani itakaa nao. Kama hawatawakaribisha, baraka yenu itarudi kwenu.

decisions.choice: your peace: the greeting of peace, a blessing of God's wholeness and well-being
decisions.reason: The greeting "peace" was a prayer for God's good on the household. Spoken by Jesus's messengers, it is more than a custom.

decisions.choice: let your peace return to you: the blessing does not rest on those who refuse it
alternatives: the disciples must take back their words
decisions.reason: A blessing is pictured as going out and, if not received, coming back to the one who gave it.

decisions.choice: welcome you
decisions.reason: Readable says what being worthy means, as in 10:11.

decisions.choice: la paz de ustedes | vuestra paz (L); la paz que ustedes le desean (B, R)
decisions.reason: With "ustedes", "su paz" could be read as the house's own peace. "La paz de ustedes" and "la paz que ustedes le desean" make clear it is the messengers' greeting (meaning decision m1); with "vosotros", "vuestra paz" is already clear.

source.text: καὶ ὃς ἂν μὴ δέξηται ὑμᾶς μηδὲ ἀκούσῃ τοὺς λόγους ὑμῶν, ἐξερχόμενοι ἔξω τῆς οἰκίας ἢ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης ἐκτινάξατε τὸν κονιορτὸν τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And whoever not receives you nor hears the words of you, going out outside of the house or of the town that shake off the dust of the feet of you.

en.L: And whoever does not receive you nor listen to your words, as you go out of that house or town, shake off the dust of your feet.
en.B: Some will not receive you or listen to your message. When you leave that house or that town, shake the dust from your feet.
en.R: Some people will not welcome you or listen to you. When you leave their house or town, shake the dust off your feet. This will be a warning to them.

es.L: Y quien no {{plural_you:los|os}} reciba ni escuche {{plural_you:las palabras de ustedes|vuestras palabras}}, al salir fuera de aquella casa o ciudad, {{plural_you:sacúdanse|sacudíos}} el polvo de los pies.
es.B: Habrá quienes no {{plural_you:los|os}} reciban ni quieran oír lo que {{plural_you:ustedes dicen|vosotros decís}}. Al salir de esa casa o de esa ciudad, {{plural_you:sacúdanse|sacudíos}} el polvo de los pies.
es.R: Habrá gente que no {{plural_you:los|os}} reciba bien ni {{plural_you:los|os}} escuche. Cuando {{plural_you:salgan|salgáis}} de su casa o de su ciudad, {{plural_you:sacúdanse|sacudíos}} el polvo de los pies. Será una advertencia para ellos.

sw.L: Na yeyote asiyewapokea wala kusikiliza maneno yenu, mkitoka nje ya nyumba hiyo au mji huo, kung'uteni vumbi la miguuni mwenu.
sw.B: Wengine hawatawapokea wala kusikiliza ujumbe wenu. Mnapoondoka katika nyumba hiyo au mji huo, kung'uteni vumbi kutoka miguuni mwenu.
sw.R: Watu wengine hawatawakaribisha wala kuwasikiliza. Mnapoondoka nyumbani kwao au mjini kwao, kung'uteni vumbi kutoka miguuni mwenu. Hilo litakuwa onyo kwao.

decisions.choice: shake off the dust: a sign that you are done with that place and it must answer for itself
decisions.reason: Paul and Barnabas do this in Acts 13:51. It shows that the messengers have done their part and leave the refusal to God's judgment (10:15).

decisions.choice: whoever does not receive you: a person or a whole town
decisions.reason: The next words speak of a house or a town, so a whole place may refuse.

decisions.choice: This will be a warning to them.
decisions.reason: Readable states what the gesture meant.

source.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται γῇ Σοδόμων καὶ Γομόρρων ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ.

records.literal_gloss: Truly I say to you, more tolerable it will be for land of Sodom and Gomorrah in day of judgment than for the town that.

en.L: Truly I tell you, it will be more bearable for [the] land of Sodom and Gomorrah on [the] day of judgment than for that town.
en.B: Truly I tell you, on the day of judgment the land of Sodom and Gomorrah will fare better than that town.
en.R: I tell you the truth, on the day God judges all people, Sodom and Gomorrah will be punished less than that town.

es.L: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: más tolerable será para [la] tierra de Sodoma y Gomorra en [el] día del juicio que para aquella ciudad.
es.B: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que en el día del juicio la región de Sodoma y Gomorra saldrá mejor parada que esa ciudad.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: el día en que Dios juzgue a todos, Sodoma y Gomorra recibirán un castigo menor que esa ciudad.

sw.L: Kweli nawaambia, hali itavumilika zaidi kwa nchi ya Sodoma na Gomora katika siku ya hukumu kuliko kwa mji ule.
sw.B: Kweli nawaambia, siku ya hukumu nchi ya Sodoma na Gomora itapata nafuu kuliko mji huo.
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli, siku ambayo Mungu atawahukumu watu wote, Sodoma na Gomora zitaadhibiwa kidogo kuliko mji huo.

decisions.choice: Sodom and Gomorrah: the cities God destroyed for their wickedness (Genesis 19)
decisions.reason: They were the byword for sin and judgment (Isaiah 1:9; Jude 7). A town that turns away God's messengers is worse off than they.

decisions.choice: more bearable: judgment will be heavier for those who refused greater light
decisions.reason: The comparison implies degrees of judgment, as in 11:22-24.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:18, the solemn opening is given in the same words at each level.

decisions.choice: will be punished less (R)
decisions.reason: Readable states the comparison plainly.

decisions.choice: En verdad les digo (L, B); Les digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts for the single "amen" that opens a solemn saying.

decisions.choice: Kweli nawaambia (L, B); Nawaambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts for the single "amen" that opens a solemn saying.

source.text: Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς ὡς πρόβατα ἐν μέσῳ λύκων· γίνεσθε οὖν φρόνιμοι ὡς οἱ ὄφεις καὶ ἀκέραιοι ὡς αἱ περιστεραί.

records.literal_gloss: Behold, I send out you as sheep in midst of wolves; be therefore shrewd as the serpents and innocent as the doves.

en.L: Look, I send you out as sheep in [the] midst of wolves; so be shrewd as the serpents and innocent as the doves.
en.B: Remember, I am the one sending you out, like sheep with wolves all around. So be shrewd like snakes, yet harmless like doves.
en.R: Listen! When I send you out, you will be like sheep with wolves all around them. So be careful and clever, like snakes. But be pure and do no wrong, like doves.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, yo {{plural_you:los|os}} envío como ovejas en medio de lobos; {{plural_you:sean|sed}}, pues, sagaces como las serpientes y puros como las palomas.
es.B: {{plural_you:Recuerden|Recordad}} que soy yo quien {{plural_you:los|os}} envía, como ovejas rodeadas de lobos. Por eso, {{plural_you:sean|sed}} sagaces como las serpientes, pero sin malicia, como las palomas.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! Cuando yo {{plural_you:los|os}} envíe, {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} como ovejas rodeadas de lobos. Así que {{plural_you:sean|sed}} prudentes y listos, como las serpientes. Pero {{plural_you:sean|sed}} puros y no {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} nada malo, como las palomas.

sw.L: Tazama, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninawapeleka kama kondoo katikati ya mbwa mwitu; kwa hiyo kuweni werevu kama nyoka na wasio na hila kama njiwa.
sw.B: Kumbukeni, ni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninayewatuma, kama kondoo waliozungukwa na mbwa mwitu. Kwa hiyo kuweni macho na werevu kama nyoka, lakini wasio na madhara kama njiwa.
sw.R: Sikilizeni! Ninapowatuma, mtakuwa kama kondoo waliozungukwa na mbwa mwitu. Kwa hiyo kuweni waangalifu na werevu kama nyoka. Lakini kuweni safi na msifanye kosa lolote, kama njiwa.

decisions.choice: sheep among wolves: defenseless people among those who will attack them
decisions.reason: The wolves are the persecutors of 10:17-23. The picture stresses danger and dependence on the shepherd who sends them.

decisions.choice: shrewd: wise and alert to danger; innocent: pure, without guile or harm
decisions.reason: The first word is used of sensible people (7:24; 25:2). The second means unmixed, with no evil in it. They must see danger clearly but never do wrong.

decisions.choice: I send you: the pronoun is stressed
decisions.reason: Jesus stresses that he himself sends them. That is their comfort in danger.

decisions.choice: look (L); remember (B); listen (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: sagaces; puros (L), sin malicia (B)
decisions.reason: Shrewd means wise and alert to danger, and innocent means without guile or harm (meaning decision m2). Spanish "prudente" now means mainly cautious, and "sencillo" can suggest naive, so Literal and Balanced use "sagaces" and "puros" or "sin malicia".

decisions.choice: Miren | Mirad (L); Recuerden (B); Escuchen (R)
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the Greek "look" is "mira" at Literal. Here Jesus is speaking to the Twelve, and Spanish addresses a group in the plural, so Literal says "miren" or "mirad"; Balanced and Readable reword it as the English does.

decisions.choice: werevu; wasio na hila (L), wasio na madhara (B)
decisions.reason: Shrewd means wise and alert to danger, and innocent means without guile or harm (meaning decision m2). "Werevu" is cleverness that sees danger; "wapole" (gentle) would lose the sense of being free of deceit.

source.text: προσέχετε δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· παραδώσουσιν γὰρ ὑμᾶς εἰς συνέδρια, καὶ ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν μαστιγώσουσιν ὑμᾶς·

records.literal_gloss: Beware but of the men; they will hand over for you to councils, and in the synagogues of them they will flog you;

en.L: But beware of {{gender:people|men}}; for they will hand you over to councils, and in their synagogues they will flog you;
en.B: Be on guard against people. They will hand you over to local councils and whip you in their synagogues.
en.R: Be careful, because people will arrest you and take you to their courts. They will beat you with whips in their meeting places.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} cuidado con {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}, pues {{plural_you:los|os}} entregarán a tribunales, y en sus sinagogas {{plural_you:los|os}} flagelarán;
es.B: {{plural_you:Estén|Estad}} en guardia frente a la gente. {{plural_you:Los|Os}} entregarán a los tribunales locales y {{plural_you:los|os}} azotarán en sus sinagogas.
es.R: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado, porque la gente {{plural_you:los|os}} arrestará y {{plural_you:los|os}} llevará a sus tribunales. {{plural_you:Los|Os}} golpearán con látigos en sus lugares de reunión.

sw.L: Lakini jilindeni dhidi ya watu; kwa maana watawakabidhi kwa mabaraza, na ndani ya sinagogi zao watawacharaza viboko;
sw.B: Kuweni macho na watu. Watawakabidhi kwa mabaraza ya mahali, na kuwachapa viboko katika sinagogi zao.
sw.R: Kuweni waangalifu, kwa sababu watu watawakamata na kuwapeleka kwenye mahakama zao. Watawapiga mijeledi katika nyumba zao za ibada.

decisions.choice: councils and synagogues: local Jewish courts and the discipline they gave
decisions.reason: Towns had local councils, and synagogues could punish by flogging, up to forty lashes (Deuteronomy 25:3). Paul received thirty-nine lashes five times (2 Corinthians 11:24).

decisions.choice: hand you over: the word used of Judas and of Jesus's arrest
decisions.reason: The disciples will go through what their master goes through (10:4; 17:22; 20:18-19).

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means people in general, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: meeting places
decisions.reason: Readable describes the synagogue, as in 4:23.

decisions.choice: {{gender:la gente|los hombres}} (L)
decisions.reason: As in English: the word means people, men and women, and Spanish has both wordings, so Literal offers the traditional "los hombres" as the alternative. Balanced and Readable say "la gente".

decisions.choice: watu, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "men" as a traditional alternative. Swahili "watu" already means people, men and women, and "wanaume" would mean males only, so there is no span.

source.text: καὶ ἐπὶ ἡγεμόνας δὲ καὶ βασιλεῖς ἀχθήσεσθε ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν.

records.literal_gloss: and before governors and also kings you will be brought on account of me for a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.

en.L: and you will be brought before governors and also kings for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.
en.B: Because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} they will take you to stand before governors and kings. There you will bear witness to them and to the Gentiles.
en.R: Because you follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you will have to stand in front of governors and kings. Then you will tell them, and people who are not Jews, about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: y también delante de gobernadores y reyes {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} conducidos a causa de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, como testimonio para ellos y para los gentiles.
es.B: Por causa {{deity_pronoun:mía|Mía}} {{plural_you:los|os}} llevarán ante gobernadores y reyes. Allí {{plural_you:darán|daréis}} testimonio ante ellos y ante los gentiles.
es.R: Como {{plural_you:ustedes me siguen|vosotros me seguís}}, {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} que presentarse ante gobernadores y reyes. Entonces les {{plural_you:hablarán|hablaréis}} de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} a ellos y a la gente que no es judía.

sw.L: na tena mbele ya magavana na wafalme mtafikishwa kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, kwa ushuhuda kwao na kwa watu wa mataifa.
sw.B: Kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} mtapelekwa mbele ya magavana na wafalme. Huko mtatoa ushuhuda mbele yao na mbele ya watu wa mataifa.
sw.R: Kwa kuwa mnanifuata, mtalazimika kusimama mbele ya watawala na wafalme. Ndipo mtawaeleza habari {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, wao na watu wasio Wayahudi.

decisions.choice: governors and kings: Roman governors such as Pilate, and rulers such as the Herods
decisions.reason: Pilate was governor of Judea (27:2). Acts tells of apostles before Herod Agrippa, Felix, Festus and Agrippa II (Acts 12; 24-26).

decisions.choice: a testimony to them and to the Gentiles: a witness given before them
decisions.reason: The words can mean a witness to them or against them. Their trials become a chance to speak about Jesus, which also leaves those who reject him without excuse.

decisions.choice: them: the rulers, and perhaps the Jewish courts of 10:17
decisions.reason: "Them" stands beside "the Gentiles", so it likely points back to the rulers and the councils.

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable says who the Gentiles are, as in 4:15.

decisions.choice: tell them ... about me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the testimony is about.

source.text: ὅταν δὲ παραδῶσιν ὑμᾶς, μὴ μεριμνήσητε πῶς ἢ τί λαλήσητε· δοθήσεται γὰρ ὑμῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τί λαλήσητε·

records.literal_gloss: When but they hand over you, not be anxious how or what you should speak; it will be given for to you in that the hour what you should speak;

en.L: But when they hand you over, do not be anxious how or what you are to speak; for what you are to speak will be given to you in that hour;
en.B: But when you are handed over, do not be anxious over how to answer or what to say. In that hour you will be given the words to speak.
en.R: When people arrest you, do not worry ahead of time about what to say. God will give you the right words when you need them.

es.L: Y cuando {{plural_you:los|os}} entreguen, no {{plural_you:se inquieten|os inquietéis}} [pensando] cómo o qué {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}}; pues en aquel momento se {{plural_you:les|os}} dará qué decir;
es.B: Pero cuando {{plural_you:los|os}} entreguen, no {{plural_you:se angustien|os angustiéis}} por cómo responder o qué decir. En ese momento se {{plural_you:les|os}} darán las palabras.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:los|os}} arresten, no {{plural_you:se preocupen|os preocupéis}} antes de tiempo por lo que {{plural_you:van|vais}} a decir. Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} dará las palabras justas cuando las {{plural_you:necesiten|necesitéis}}.

sw.L: Na wakati watakapowakabidhi, msihangaike mtasemaje au mtasema nini; kwa maana katika saa hiyo mtajaliwa la kusema;
sw.B: Lakini mtakapokabidhiwa, msihangaike juu ya jinsi ya kujibu au nini cha kusema. Saa hiyo mtapewa maneno ya kusema.
sw.R: Watu watakapowakamata, msisumbuke mapema juu ya mtakachosema. Mungu atawapa maneno yanayofaa wakati mtakapoyahitaji.

decisions.choice: it will be given: by God
decisions.reason: The passive points to God, as 10:20 makes plain.

decisions.choice: be anxious: worry, as in 6:25-34
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in the Sermon on the Mount. Jesus forbids fearful worry, not thought.

decisions.choice: God will give you
alternatives: it will be given to you
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the giver.

source.text: οὐ γὰρ ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ λαλοῦντες ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τὸ λαλοῦν ἐν ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: not for you are the speaking but the Spirit of the Father of you the speaking in you.

en.L: for you are not the ones speaking, but the Spirit of your Father [is the one] speaking in you.
en.B: The speaker will not be you; it will be your Father's Spirit speaking in you.
en.R: The words will not really come from you. Your Father's Spirit will speak through you.

es.L: pues quienes hablan no {{plural_you:son ustedes|sois vosotros}}, sino el Espíritu de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre, [que es] el que habla en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: El que hablará no {{plural_you:serán ustedes|seréis vosotros}}; será el Espíritu de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre el que hable en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: En realidad, las palabras no saldrán de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. El Espíritu de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre hablará por medio de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: kwa maana wanaosema si ninyi, bali Roho wa Baba yenu ndiye anayesema ndani yenu.
sw.B: Atakayesema si ninyi; atakuwa Roho wa Baba yenu akisema ndani yenu.
sw.R: Maneno hayo hayatatoka kwenu hasa. Roho wa Baba yenu atasema kupitia kwenu.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of your Father: God's Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: This phrase is found only here. It ties the Spirit to the Father who cares for them (10:29-31).

decisions.choice: in you: within you and through you
decisions.reason: The Spirit speaks from within the disciple; the words come through the disciple's own mouth.

source.text: παραδώσει δὲ ἀδελφὸς ἀδελφὸν εἰς θάνατον καὶ πατὴρ τέκνον, καὶ ἐπαναστήσονται τέκνα ἐπὶ γονεῖς καὶ θανατώσουσιν αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: Will hand over and brother brother to death and father child, and will rise up children against parents and will put to death them.

en.L: And brother will hand over brother to death, and father child, and children will rise up against parents and put them to death.
en.B: One brother will hand another over to be killed, and a father his own child. Children will turn on their parents and send them to their death.
en.R: Brothers will hand each other over to be killed. Fathers will do this to their children. Children will turn against their parents and have them killed.

es.L: Y entregará el hermano al hermano a [la] muerte, y el padre al hijo, y se rebelarán hijos contra padres y les darán muerte.
es.B: Un hermano entregará a otro para que lo maten, y un padre a su propio hijo. Los hijos se volverán contra sus padres y los mandarán a la muerte.
es.R: Habrá hermanos que se entregarán unos a otros para que los maten. Habrá padres que harán lo mismo con sus hijos. Habrá hijos que se pondrán en contra de sus padres y harán que los maten.

sw.L: Na ndugu atamkabidhi ndugu auawe, na baba [atamkabidhi] mtoto, na watoto wataasi dhidi ya wazazi na kuwaua.
sw.B: Ndugu atamkabidhi ndugu yake ili auawe, na baba atamkabidhi mtoto wake. Watoto watawageuka wazazi wao na kuwapeleka wauawe.
sw.R: Ndugu watakabidhiana ili wauawe. Baba watawafanyia watoto wao vivyo hivyo. Watoto watawageuka wazazi wao na kuwafanya wauawe.

decisions.choice: children against parents: Micah 7:6
decisions.reason: Micah describes a time when families turn on each other. Jesus quotes it more fully in 10:35-36.

decisions.choice: put them to death: cause them to be executed by handing them over
alternatives: kill them with their own hands
decisions.reason: The children bring about their parents' death by denouncing them.

decisions.choice: brother: a brother by birth
decisions.reason: The verse is about members of one family, so the words name actual relatives.

source.text: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου· ὁ δὲ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος οὗτος σωθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: And you will be being hated by all because of the name of me; the but having endured to end, this one will be saved.

en.L: And you will be hated by all because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name; but the one who endures to [the] end, this [one] will be saved.
en.B: Everyone will hate you because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. But whoever holds out to the end will be saved.
en.R: Everyone will hate you because you belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. But anyone who stays faithful to the end will be saved.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:estarán|estaréis}} siendo odiados por todos a causa de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre; pero quien resista hasta [el] fin, ese será salvado.
es.B: Todos {{plural_you:los|os}} odiarán por causa de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre. Pero el que se mantenga firme hasta el final se salvará.
es.R: Todos {{plural_you:los|os}} odiarán porque {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} {{deity_pronoun:míos|Míos}}. Pero quien se mantenga fiel hasta el final será salvado.

sw.L: Nanyi mtakuwa mkichukiwa na wote kwa sababu ya jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}; lakini yeye atakayevumilia hadi mwisho, huyo ataokolewa.
sw.B: Watu wote watawachukia kwa sababu ya jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. Lakini yeyote atakayeshikilia imara hadi mwisho ataokolewa.
sw.R: Kila mtu atawachukia kwa sababu ninyi ni {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. Lakini yeyote atakayebaki mwaminifu hadi mwisho ataokolewa.

decisions.choice: because of my name: because you belong to me
alternatives: because you use my name in prayer
decisions.reason: A name stands for the person. They are hated for being his.

decisions.choice: to the end: to the end of the trial, even if it brings death
alternatives: to the end of the age only
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "to the very end" or "to the end of the age" (24:13-14). Either way, one must hold firm however long the trouble lasts.

decisions.choice: will be saved: rescued for life in God's kingdom
decisions.reason: Some will be put to death (10:21), so this is rescue beyond death, as in 10:39.

decisions.choice: stays faithful
decisions.reason: Readable says what enduring means here.

source.text: ὅταν δὲ διώκωσιν ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ, φεύγετε εἰς τὴν ἑτέραν· ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ τελέσητε τὰς πόλεις τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

records.literal_gloss: When but they persecute you in the town this, flee into the other; truly for I say to you, not not you will finish the towns of Israel until comes the Son of the Man.

en.L: But whenever they persecute you in this town, flee to the other; for truly I tell you, you will not finish the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.
en.B: If they hunt you down in one town, escape to the next. Truly I tell you, the Son of Man will come before you have completed your work in the towns of Israel.
en.R: When people in one town attack you, escape to another town. I tell you the truth, the Son of Man will come before you have finished going to all the towns of Israel.

es.L: Y cuando {{plural_you:los|os}} persigan en esta ciudad, {{plural_you:huyan|huid}} a la otra; porque en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: no {{plural_you:terminarán|terminaréis}} las ciudades de Israel antes de que venga el Hijo del Hombre.
es.B: Si {{plural_you:los|os}} acosan en una ciudad, {{plural_you:escapen|escapad}} a la siguiente. En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que el Hijo del Hombre vendrá antes de que {{plural_you:hayan|hayáis}} terminado {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} trabajo en las ciudades de Israel.
es.R: Cuando la gente de una ciudad {{plural_you:los|os}} ataque, {{plural_you:escapen|escapad}} a otra ciudad. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: el Hijo del Hombre vendrá antes de que {{plural_you:hayan|hayáis}} ido a todas las ciudades de Israel.

sw.L: Na wakati wowote watakapowatesa katika mji huu, kimbieni hadi ule mwingine; kwa maana kweli nawaambia, hakika hamtamaliza miji ya Israeli mpaka Mwana wa Adamu atakapokuja.
sw.B: Wakiwawinda katika mji mmoja, kimbilieni mji unaofuata. Kweli nawaambia, Mwana wa Adamu atakuja kabla hamjamaliza kazi yenu katika miji ya Israeli.
sw.R: Watu wa mji mmoja wakiwashambulia, kimbilieni mji mwingine. Nawaambia ukweli, Mwana wa Adamu atakuja kabla hamjamaliza kwenda katika miji yote ya Israeli.

decisions.choice: before the Son of Man comes: the meaning is debated
alternatives: his coming at the end of the age
his coming in judgment on Jerusalem in AD 70
his joining the twelve during this mission
decisions.reason: The words recall Daniel 7:13, where one like a son of man comes to God and receives the kingdom. Some take it of the end of the age, with the mission to Israel going on until then; others of Jesus's resurrection and authority (28:18) or of the judgment on Jerusalem (24:30, 34). The translation keeps the open wording.

decisions.choice: finish the towns of Israel: complete the mission to them, or run out of places to flee
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring to an end. In context it may mean they will not finish preaching in Israel, or not run out of towns to flee to.

decisions.choice: persecute: pursue and harass
decisions.reason: The verb means to chase or pursue, and so to persecute (5:10-12).

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:18, the solemn opening is given in the same words at each level.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre
decisions.reason: The title used throughout the New Testament drafts, with both nouns capitalised as a title.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu
decisions.reason: The settled Swahili title, used throughout the New Testament drafts (Adamu is also "humankind"); never under the gender setting.
